newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Banned Indonesian writer fails to regain home.
newsitem.headline: Banned Indonesian writer fails to regain home.

text.p: Indonesian writer Pramoedya Ananta Toer, most of whose works are banned in his homeland, failed on Tuesday to regain his Jakarta home more than three decades after it was confiscated by the military.

A panel of three judges in the Central Jakarta State Court ruled against Pramoedya in his case against the Department of Defence and Security and Lieutenant-Colonel Rachmad Sidarta, the retired officer occupying the house.

Lawyers for the 70-year-old Pramoedya had asked the court to return the house and for the defendants to pay 450 million rupiah ($193,133) in back rent since it was seized in the wake of the abortive communist coup in 1965.
But judges dismissed the case on a technicality saying Pramoedya should have sued the Jakarta military commander who was the responsible party. His lawyers said they would appeal.
Pramoedya was detained by military and police after his house was attacked by a mob of stone-throwing youths in October 1965 and has not set foot in it since.
The critically acclaimed novelist spent 14 years in jail, including 10 on the prison island of Buru where he wrote four of his more than 30 books, most of which are banned in Indonesia.

Like many political prisoners of the period, Pramoedya was never charged but imprisoned because of his links with Lekra, the people's cultural institute of the banned Indonesian Communist Party (PKI).
In 1995, Pramoedya was awarded the Ramon Magsaysay prize for journalism and literature from the Philippines.
